text:
elaine: Heads up — after yesterday's scheduler tweak I'm seeing a 12-18% median latency jump on mid-length (512-1024) seqs in canary. nvprof/nsys traces show a different kernel being chosen for the same shape. anyone else? :eyes:
samir: saw similar in the nightly runs. thought it was noise but consistent across GPUs.
dilip: can you paste the trace snippets?
elaine: short dump from nsys (sanitized):
```
# nsys profile --output=canary-2026-03-16.nsys --trace=cuda,cudnn --sample=none ./runner --workload=llama-7b --seq=768
Timeline: 0ms   kernel_A (conv-fused)  -> 1ms   kernel_B (attention-opt) -> 2ms kernel_C (kv-update)
Hotspots: kernel_B dominates (72% GPU time) vs expected kernel_A in baseline
```
elaine: kernel_B has lower theoretical occupancy for that shape, hence the perf drop.
kai: that matches the perf tests I ran locally. My hypothesis: new scheduler change allowed probing of variant selector that prefers kernel_B when batch packing hits a specific remainder.
samir: can we reproduce minimal repro and bisect? I can run binary search on commit range.
dilip: I started a quick bisection on the canary branch: `git bisect start; git bisect bad HEAD; git bisect good v1.20.3`
perf-bot: bisect job queued #8420. Will run traces on every step.
elaine: notes from manual compare: baseline (pre-change) kernel timeline: kernel_A -> kv-update -> done. after-change: kernel_probe -> kernel_B -> kv-update. The probe path switches the kernel selector table.
kai: I dumped the selector table state: `selector_table[(seq=768, bs=6)] = variant_index=3` after-change vs `variant_index=1` before-change.
samir: interesting. variant_index=3 corresponds to kernel_B mapping in our variant registry. Where does selector get updated?
dilip: it looks like the packing heuristic (batcher) sets a transient 'probe' flag when partial fill > 0.6; that flag triggers an extra profiling sample which writes to selector cache. The commit 7f2a8c4 changed the probe threshold to 0.6 from 0.8.
elaine: aha. so more probes => selector may learn an unrepresentative mapping under ephemeral packing patterns.
kai: reproduce steps I used:
```
# tiny repro harness
python tools/repro_kernel_selector.py --model llama-7b --seq 768 --clients 6 --seed 42 --runs 400 --save selector_dump.json
# compare dumps pre/post
jq '.selector["768",6]' selector_dump.json
```
elaine: after running the harness I get stable flip to variant 3 within ~40 runs. pre-change stays at variant 1.
samir: bisect found a likely culprit: 7f2a8c4 (batcher: reduce probe threshold). Suspect change introduced over-eager sampling.
dilip: rolling patch: revert threshold to 0.8 and add decay for transient samples. small change. draft PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4987
ei: (from perf-bot) CI nsys traces attached to PR show median latency restored to baseline, kernel timeline matches kernel_A as dominant.
kai: left one comment on PR asking for an E2E test: add a reproducible selector harness in CI with seq=768 and assert stable mapping.
elaine: agreed. also add a debug-only nvtx marker around selector updates so we can correlate future traces.
samir: thanks folks — thumbs-up to merge once CI passes. leaving the bisect artifacts in `s3://redwood-perf/bisect/2765437890/`
dilip: follow-up: we should also add a guard that ignores single-sample updates until count >= N (N=5). PR updated.
elaine: deployed revert to canary stack; monitoring now. will report if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
